sections.title: 1. Super-speciality exposure
sections.summary: Both the NMC MD and the NBEMS DNB schedules assume months in cardiac, neuro, paediatric, obstetric and ICU theatres. A DNB hospital only has to run general surgery, ortho/trauma, ENT, OBG and a pain clinic in-house, so check how the missing areas are covered.

points.text: NMC MD Anaesthesiology (CBME) suggested rotation: General Surgery 6 mo, Ortho/Trauma/Casualty 3, Gynae 3, Obstetrics 3, ICU 4, ENT 2, CTVS 2, Neurosurgery 2, Paediatric Surgery 2, Pain 1, Recovery 1, Urology/Eye/Dental/Burns 1 each. Radiology, radiotherapy, ECT and cath lab are also listed, with no set duration.
NMC ICU rule: 4 months of ICU posting, 2 under supervision in the early years and 2 independently in the last six months.

NBEMS DNB Anaesthesia guideline (archived 2021 version on nbe.edu.in): CTVS/cath lab 2 mo, Neurosurgery 3, Paediatric Surgery 2, Obstetrics/labour room 3, ICU 4, Pain Clinic 1, Ortho/Trauma/EM 4, plus 6 organ-transplant cases.
The DNB curriculum puts cardiac, neuro and paediatric cases in year 3: the resident should be able to plan and give anaesthesia for them under graded supervision.

To be accredited for DNB Anaesthesiology, a hospital needs a 10-bed ICU and in-house General Surgery, Ortho/Trauma/EM, ENT, OBG and a Pain Clinic. Cardiac, neuro, paediatric and transplant work are not required.
A DNB department missing a sub-speciality may rotate trainees to another NMC/NBEMS-recognised centre for up to 6 months under an MoU. Core areas cannot be rotated out.
Cardiac, Neuro, Paediatric, Onco, Transplant and Trauma Anaesthesia & Critical Care each exist as NBEMS DrNB/FNB super-speciality courses. Early exposure helps you choose a later DM/DrNB/FNB.
Peripheral GMCs may list no super-speciality departments at all. For example, GMC Ratlam's official department list has no cardiology, CTVS, neurosurgery, urology or paediatric surgery.
Benchmark: KEM Mumbai performed a heart transplant in 2024 and runs a liver transplant unit. Grant GMC/JJ has had a CVTS department since 1961.
A seat's DM/MCh courses are a rough guide to which super-specialities are active. The official MCC 2025 seat matrix lists them by institute.

red_flags: No CTVS, neurosurgery or paediatric surgery department on the college/hospital website, and no named outside-posting centre
Outside postings that exist only on paper, or that the resident must arrange (and pay for) personally
DNB hospital with no MoU for sub-speciality rotation
ICU run by another department, with anaesthesia residents only doing OT work
Transplant or cardiac programme that is 'starting soon' or does a handful of cases a year
ask_seniors: Which of cardiac, neuro, paeds, transplant and onco did you actually rotate through, for how many months, and where?
How many open-heart cases and craniotomies did you personally do or observe last year?
Is labour analgesia a running service, and do residents give the epidurals?
Is there a pain clinic with procedures (blocks, RF), or only OPD?
For outside postings: who arranges them, is stipend paid during them, and are they ever cancelled?

sections.title: 2. Hands-on training
sections.summary: NBEMS gives minimum logbook numbers for DNB; the NMC MD guideline lists the procedures but sets no counts. Either way, what matters is how many blocks, central lines and difficult airways you get to do yourself.

points.text: DNB minimum logbook (regional): 50 spinals, 50 lumbar epidurals, 30 caudals, 20 CSE, 10 brachial plexus (plus 5 observed), 5+5 sciatic/femoral, 10 other peripheral nerve blocks.

DNB minimum logbook (lines/cases): IJV 10 done + 10 observed, subclavian 10+10, arterial line 10+10, 100 ASA I cases independently, 20 difficult-airway drills; open heart, closed heart, craniotomy, spine and joint replacement 10 each (observed); transplant 5 (observed); labour analgesia 10 (observed).
Without the logbook, the DNB final result is not declared. The supervisor certifies it and the head of the institution countersigns.
NMC MD: lists 19 procedures residents must be able to perform, sets no minimum numbers, and requires logbooks to be maintained and periodically assessed by faculty.
DNB trainees must also clear a thesis and a minimum number of Formative Assessment Tests (FATs) before they can sit the final.
NMC District Residency Programme: MD/MS residents do 3 months in a district hospital (semesters 3–5) on full stipend. This is time away from tertiary OTs.

Model differences (inference, not measured): a busy government college gives volume and emergency cases with thinner supervision. A corporate DNB gives closer consultant supervision with fewer cases per trainee. NBEMS caps trainees per consultant (e.g. 1 senior + 1 junior consultant gets 1 post-MBBS seat).
No institute in the target list publishes resident case logs or block volumes, so this can only be checked with seniors.

red_flags: Residents only 'observe' spinals or central lines in year 2
Consultants give every block themselves (common in fee-for-service corporate set-ups)
No ultrasound machine for blocks/lines, or one machine shared across all OTs
Logbook signed in bulk at the end of the course instead of after each posting
Thesis guide unavailable, which delays DNB eligibility
ask_seniors: By the end of year 1, how many spinals, epidurals and intubations had you done independently?
Do juniors give ultrasound-guided blocks, and how many per month?
Who puts in central and arterial lines in OT and ICU, residents or consultants?
Is there a difficult-airway cart, video laryngoscope and fibreoptic scope that residents actually use?
Are there simulation, airway or regional workshops (ISA/AORA) and does the department fund them?

sections.title: 3. Working hours & toxicity
sections.summary: The legal limits are not being enforced. Anaesthesia residents cover OT lists, ICU and emergency calls, so duty patterns vary widely by department and must be checked with current residents.

points.text: Central Residency Scheme 1992: maximum 12 hours a day and 48 hours a week. NMC PGMER-2023 only says 'reasonable working hours'.
PGMER-2023 does guarantee one weekly holiday, 20 days' paid casual leave a year, 5 days' academic leave, and stipend at government-college rates.
NMC National Task Force (2024) recommended a cap of 74 hours a week, no shift longer than 24 hours, and one day off a week. It found back-to-back 24-hour duties, sometimes 3–5 in a row.
NMC has told the Supreme Court that enforcing duty hours is the states' job.
Supreme Court (UDF PIL seeking enforcement of the 12h/48h limits): NMC has filed its affidavit, the Health Ministry has been asked for its reply, and the next hearing is listed for 27 Oct 2026.

Maharashtra, 2 Apr 2026: the government ordered all GMCs to cap resident duty at 48 hours a week and 12 hours a day. An IGGMC Nagpur notice added no emergency duty for JR-1s in their first 6 months. No source confirms it is being enforced.
Anecdotal (RDA quotes in news, 2025): 48-hour shifts called 'standard' at LNJP/MAMC, and 24–36-hour shifts without rest rooms at RML Delhi.
Maharashtra MARD strikes (2025–26) were mostly about safety, harassment and a homoeopathy rule, not hours, but they still disrupted training.
Stipend non-payment is a form of toxicity. In an NMC 2023 survey, 2,110 private-college PG students reported receiving no stipend.
No anaesthesia-specific duty-hour data (call frequency, post-call off) was found for any institute. Only seniors can tell you this.

red_flags: Back-to-back 24-hour calls, or no post-call off after a night in ICU or emergency
JR-1s left alone in the emergency OT or ICU at night
Stipend delayed by months, or 'returned' to management
News of harassment, suicide or an MPHRC/court case involving the department
Leave or thesis approval used as a threat (as alleged in the GMC Bhopal 2024 plea)
ask_seniors: How many 24-hour calls a month, and is the next day off?
Who covers the emergency OT and ICU at night, and is a consultant physically present?
Is the weekly off actually given?
Is the stipend paid on time and in full, and how much is it?
Has anyone left the course in the last 3 years, and why?
How does the HoD handle mistakes and leave requests?

sections.title: 4. DNB pass rate
sections.summary: NBEMS does not publish pass rates by institute or by specialty. Judge a DNB hospital through proxies: seat count, how stable the faculty is, and how the last batches did in the exam.

points.text: DNB final results are declared only as PASS/FAIL. Marks are visible only to each candidate through their login, so there is no institute-wise data.
Theory is 4 papers of 100 marks with a 200/400 aggregate needed. Practical is OSCE-format, with limited attempts before you must re-sit theory.
No official national DNB Anaesthesiology pass percentage was found. One blog claims about 48% (range 42–60%) with no source, so treat it as unreliable.
A 2021 report found pass rates under 40% in several DNB specialties (it gave no figure for anaesthesia).
NBEMS accreditation depends on faculty and infrastructure, not exam results. If faculty leave and are not replaced, accreditation can be withdrawn and trainees relocated.
Precedent: in Jan 2025 NBEMS withdrew allotted DNB General Surgery seats at Ruby General Hospital, Kolkata, after faculty resigned.

Seats granted depend on the number of senior/junior consultants, so a department with 1 seat has 1–2 qualified faculty. More seats means a deeper faculty bench (e.g. Narayana Health Bengaluru had about 25 Round-1 DNB allotments in 2025).
The only other way to get pass data is an RTI to NBEMS, or the hospital's own unverified claims.

red_flags: 1-seat department that depends on a single senior consultant
Recent faculty exits, or 'consultant is visiting only'
Thesis submissions delayed for past batches
No regular teaching (NBEMS expects weekly case presentation, seminar and journal club)
Seniors who passed only on a 2nd or 3rd attempt, without explanation
ask_seniors: Of the last 2–3 batches, how many cleared theory and practical at the first attempt?
How many consultants are NBEMS-approved guides, and has any left recently?
Are mock exams, OSCE practice and weekly academic sessions actually held?
Was any thesis submission late, and why?
When does the hospital's accreditation expire, and has it ever been red-flagged or had seats cut?

sections.title: 5. Bond & penalty
sections.summary: These are two separate costs. A service bond is payable if you don't serve after PG. A discontinuation or seat-leaving penalty is payable if you quit midway or after a cut-off round. MCC's only penalty is forfeiting your deposit. Most figures below come from 2025 brochures, so re-check them in the 2026 documents.

points.text: MCC 2026 refundable deposit: ₹25,000 (UR/EWS AIQ), ₹10,000 (OBC/SC/ST/PwD AIQ), ₹2,00,000 (deemed). It is forfeited if you don't join a seat allotted in Round 2 or later, or if your admission is cancelled. MCC sets no bond and says bond and stipend terms are the institute's.

Maharashtra govt/municipal seats (AIQ or state quota): 1-year service bond or ₹50 lakh; ₹10 lakh for not completing the residency; a further ₹10 lakh plus a 2-year state-quota bar for letting a seat lapse. Private seats have no bond, but resigning after the cut-off costs 3 years' fees (2025 brochure).
Rajasthan (order of 1 Sep 2025): 2 years of service or a ₹50 lakh bond for Anaesthesia, plus a reported ₹10 lakh seat-leaving surety for AIQ and state seats.
Kerala (including AIQ): at least 1 year as a Senior Resident, or repay stipend plus ₹50 lakh. Vacating after the stray round costs ₹50 lakh.
Tamil Nadu (including 50% AIQ): 2 years of service; ₹40 lakh penalty for MD/MS.
Karnataka: ₹10 lakh for discontinuing a degree course, plus a 3-year PG admission bar (govt, AIQ and private seats). Reports differ on the service bond: 3 years/₹50 lakh or 1 year.
Delhi GNCTD colleges (e.g. MAMC), AIQ and state quota: 1 year of service or a ₹20 lakh PG bond, from 2025-26.
Telangana: ₹50 lakh for not completing the course, and a 1-year service bond of ₹20 lakh (degree).
UP (aggregator source, unverified): 2 years of service or ₹40 lakh, including DNB. In 2025 the DGME barred 148 candidates who did not join or left seats.
Bihar: 3 years of service or ₹25 lakh plus stipend; ₹15 lakh plus stipend for leaving a seat. West Bengal: 3 years of service; ₹5 lakh MD/MS discontinuation bond; no discontinuation bond for DNB.
DNB: hospitals may not charge a security deposit or bond. Only government hospitals may impose a service bond, and only if declared before counselling.
DNB: resigning can lead to a ban from NBEMS exams, and anyone who has joined a PG seat is ineligible for another DNB seat for that course's full duration.
NMC's Jan 2024 letter asked states to drop seat-leaving bonds. It is advisory, and most states kept them.

red_flags: A private DNB hospital asking for a deposit, bank guarantee or bond (NBEMS bars this)
Original certificates held back beyond what the brochure allows
The bond amount you are told verbally differs from MCC's 'Information about college, fee, bond' entry
Stipend you would have to repay if you leave (common in Kerala, Bihar and TN bond terms)
ask_seniors: Exactly what bond did you sign: amount, years, and where you serve?
Did the college hold your original certificates, and when did you get them back?
Can the service bond be served as a Senior Resident in a GMC, and is a post actually offered?
Has anyone paid the bond instead of serving, and how long did the paperwork take?

sections.title: MD vs DNB vs deemed vs private
sections.summary: For faculty jobs DNB counts as MD, except that DNB from a hospital under 500 beds needs one extra year of senior residency. The choice usually comes down to cost, stipend, bond and caseload.

points.text: NMC faculty regulations 2025: DNB is equivalent to MD/MS. DNB from an institution with fewer than 500 beds needs 1 extra year of senior residency in a recognised medical college before you can be an assistant professor.
DNB stipend floor (from 1 Jun 2025): ₹43k/45k/47k a month for years 1–3. Private hospitals must pay this or the state rate, whichever is higher. The NBEMS course fee is ₹1.25 lakh a year.
Govt MD (Maharashtra): tuition about ₹1.52 lakh a year. NMC filings put the state stipend benchmark at about ₹76.6k a month, but bonds are attached (see section 5).
Maharashtra private MD (FRA 2024-25): about ₹9–19 lakh a year in tuition. Colleges report paying ₹52–65k a month in stipend, below the state rate.

Deemed MD Anaesthesia: 2025 cutoffs mostly beyond AIR 42k (e.g. KMC Manipal 45,409 in R3), so the seats are reachable. Fees are about ₹20–35 lakh a year (secondary source) and the MCC deposit is ₹2 lakh.
Private DNB hospitals have no category reservation, so your OBC-NCL status only helps for AIQ, central and govt DNB seats.
2026-27 NMC seat matrix: 5,672 MD Anaesthesiology seats (Maharashtra 668). DNB Anaesthesia had about 1,030 MCC Round-1 allotments in 2025.
MD residents must do the 3-month District Residency. A DNB hospital that lacks sub-specialities can rotate trainees out for up to 6 months.

red_flags: Deemed or private college with a stipend 'as per state' on paper but a clawback in practice
DNB at a hospital under 500 beds when you want a teaching career (adds 1 year)
New college whose MD seats are only 'permitted', not yet recognised (check NMC course search)
ask_seniors: What is the real take-home stipend after any deductions or refunds?
What were the total 3-year fees, hostel and caution money?
For DNB: how many beds does the hospital have, and do graduates get SR posts in medical colleges?
Is the MD seat NMC-recognised, or only permitted?

sections.title: Counselling strategy 2026
sections.summary: Use Round 1 and Round 2 to explore, because you can leave cheaply. Treat Round 3 as final, since you cannot resign or upgrade after joining. Watch the overlap between MCC and Maharashtra rounds.

points.text: MCC 2026 AIQ Round 1: registration 12–21 Oct, choice locking 21–22 Oct, result 24 Oct, joining by 2 Nov. Round 2: 6–14 Nov. Round 3: 26 Nov–4 Dec. Stray round: 16–24 Dec. The session starts 20 Nov.
State quota per MCC's combined schedule: Round 1 runs 21 Oct–2 Nov (join by 10 Nov), Round 2 14–23 Nov, Round 3 4–12 Dec. The Maharashtra 2026 PG portal was not live as of 10 Oct.

New for 2026, Freeze: you accept the seat and join physically. Float: you join online, upload documents and request an upgrade, with no visit to the college. Upgrades through Float are possible only up to Round 3.
Round 1 has a free exit: you can skip joining and still take part in Round 2. If you take a Round 1 seat as Freeze without asking for an upgrade, you are not considered for Round 2.
Round 2 and later: if you don't join an allotted seat, you lose your deposit. You can resign Round 1 and 2 seats within the window.
Round 3 trap: once you join a Round 3 seat you cannot upgrade or resign it. Not joining means losing the deposit and being shut out of all further MCC rounds.
Stray round: open only to candidates not holding a seat. States share their Round 3 data with MCC, and anyone on a state's post-Round-3 list is removed from the AIQ stray round.

Maharashtra (2025 rules): resigning a govt seat after the cut-off costs ₹10 lakh, or ₹10 lakh plus a 2-year bar if the seat lapses; a private seat costs 3 years' fees. The state deposit was ₹12,500 (reserved, govt-only choices) or ₹1 lakh if you include private colleges.
OBC-NCL: you need a central-list certificate in MCC's Annexure-4 format, based on income for FY ending 31 Mar 2026. A state-format certificate risks losing the OBC seat.
Before choice filling, check each college's bond, fee and stipend on MCC's 'Information about college, fee, bond' page. MCC disclaims any responsibility for these terms.

red_flags: Taking a Round 3 seat 'to be safe' when a state Round 3 or stray seat would suit you better (you are locked in)
Joining a state seat after state Round 3 while hoping for the AIQ stray round (you will be removed)
Choosing Freeze in Round 1 when you still want an upgrade
Filling choices without checking each college's bond (₹10–50 lakh exposure)
Using an old or state-format OBC certificate
ask_seniors: Which round did you get this seat in, and at what rank (OBC)?
Did the college process Float online document verification smoothly last year?
Did the college or DMER delay relieving letters during upgrades?
Was the bond explained at admission, or only after joining?
